t:
(a) In General.—Section 231 of title 10, United States Code, is amended—
        (1) by redesignating subsection (e) as subsection (f); and 
        (2) by inserting after subsection (d) the following new subsection (e):“(e) Limitation on Availability of Funds for Fiscal Years Without Plan and Certification.—(1) If the Secretary of Defense does not include with the defense budget materials for a fiscal year the plan and certification under subsection (a), the Secretary of the Navy may not use more than 50 percent of the funds described in paragraph (2) during the fiscal year in which such materials are submitted until the date on which such plan and certification are submitted to the congressional defense committees.“(2) The funds described in this paragraph are funds made available to the Secretary of the Navy for operation and maintenance, Navy, for emergencies and extraordinary expenses.”.  
    (b) Conforming Amendment.—Section 12304b(i) of title 10, United States Code, is amended by striking “section 231(g)(2)” and inserting “section 231(f)(2)”.

fable.w: The section limits the Navy's use of certain funds until the Secretary of Defense submits a shipbuilding plan and certification to the congressional defense committees. The tempting reading is that submitting a plan to committees is a participatory process, but Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no rulemaking, hearing or right to sue is created.
fable.s: until the date on which such plan and certification are submitted to the congressional defense committees

qwen_block.w: This section imposes a funding limitation on the Secretary of the Navy contingent upon the submission of a plan and certification to congressional defense committees. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to or submitting documents to Congress is an intra-governmental action, not participation by outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, the public, or other non-federal entities.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of the Navy may not use more than 50 percent of the funds described in paragraph (2) during the fiscal year in which such materials are submitted until the date on which such plan and certification are submitted to the congressional defense committees

opus.w: The section limits Navy funds until the Secretary of Defense submits a plan and certification to the congressional defense committees. All the actors are inside the federal government: the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of the Navy and congressional committees. A report or submission to Congress is not participation, however procedural it sounds. No outside party is consulted or given a role in the decision.
opus.s: the Secretary of the Navy may not use more than 50 percent of the funds described in paragraph (2) during the fiscal year in which such materials are submitted until the date on which such plan and certification are submitted to the congressional defense committees.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** The section is procedural. It withholds Navy funds until a plan and certification are submitted, which could look like outside input into a funding decision. That reading fails because the only recipients are "the congressional defense committees," and Congress is inside the federal government. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and the section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue. The conforming amendment only changes a cross-reference.

Since Congress and its committees are considered inside the federal government, this interaction is intra-governmental and does not constitute participation with outside parties. There is no requirement for consultation with states, tribes, the public, or other non-federal entities.
